core.name: Animism
core.evidence: Mitchell’s faith in his father’s ability to fix the fish illustrates

confusables.name: Egocentric
confusables.reason: Egocentrism is another Piagetian early-childhood cognitive limitation, so it is tempting when a child makes an illogical claim, but it concerns perspective-taking rather than attributing life/fixability to an inanimate object.

items.notes: The item tests animism: attributing life/lifelike fixability to an inanimate object (the fish). Identification (option C) is not a close developmental near-miss in the candidate set, so it is omitted from confusables.
